episode_id: The sync conflicts. Resolve it the way this project expects. Start from upstream's dependency file and add back what I added./seed-6-lockfile_conflict-29016

reason: negative side failed: preconditions accepted 1 of 15 unrelated states (diverged seed 0 resolves to 'merge'); a precondition set that accepts unrelated states is a defect. It also accepted 1 more state(s) it must refuse: preconditions accepted 1 of 1 same-intent states (lockfile_conflict seed 2 resolves to 'keep_local', which accepts ['keep_local'], but the program implements 'take_upstream'); firing where a sibling resolution is correct is the mismatch this gate exists to refuse

refused_program.intent: Resolve a diverged sync whose dependency/lock file is changed on both sides by starting from upstream's version of that file, re-adding the lines the local branch added, and committing the merge.

postconditions.description: no merge is left in progress
postconditions.name: merge_completed

postconditions.description: the index holds no unmerged entries
postconditions.name: no_unmerged_entries

postconditions.description: upstream's commit is contained in HEAD, i.e. the sync was actually integrated
postconditions.name: upstream_is_ancestor

postconditions.description: the merged tree drops no line that upstream's version carries (upstream's file is the base of the resolution)
postconditions.name: upstream_lines_retained
postconditions.probe: ! git diff -U0 {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch} HEAD | grep -e '^-' | grep -v '^---' | grep -q .

postconditions.description: the merged tree still differs from upstream, so the local additions were added back
postconditions.name: local_additions_retained

postconditions.description: no staged, unstaged or untracked leftovers remain
postconditions.name: worktree_clean
postconditions.probe: git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && ! git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -q .

preconditions.description: the upstream remote-tracking branch exists locally
preconditions.name: upstream_ref_present

preconditions.description: HEAD and upstream each carry commits the other lacks, so a sync is pending in both directions
preconditions.name: diverged_from_upstream
preconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch}) || exit 1
[ -n "$base" ] || exit 1
[ "$(git rev-list --count {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch}..HEAD)" -ge 1 ] || exit 1
[ "$(git rev-list --count HEAD..{upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch})" -ge 1 ] || exit 1

preconditions.description: exactly one path differs from the merge base on both HEAD and upstream, i.e. there is exactly one sync-conflict candidate
preconditions.name: single_path_changed_on_both_sides
preconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch}) || exit 1
common=$(comm -12 \
  <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) \
  <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch} | tr '\0' '\n' | sort))
[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$common" | grep -c .)" -eq 1 ]

preconditions.description: no uncommitted work and no untracked files would obstruct the merge, unless a merge is already in progress
preconditions.name: clean_or_merging
preconditions.probe:
if [ -f "$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)" ]; then exit 0; fi
git diff --quiet || exit 1
git diff --cached --quiet || exit 1
! git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -q .
